headlines.title: Amazon launches in-app push against Mamdani-backed delivery bill in New York City
headlines.summary: Amazon has lobbied heavily against the proposed legislation, while New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani backed the bill earlier this year.
headlines.article_text: amazon-nyc-delivery-protection-act Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Amazon is showing pop-up notices to some users of its app and website warning against a New York City bill that aims to disrupt its contracted delivery model. A banner on its homepage states the bill, dubbed the Delivery Protection Act, "could add up to $5 per order." Amazon has lobbied heavily against the proposed legislation, while New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani backed the bill earlier this year. In this article AMZN Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT An Amazon driver loads packages into a delivery van at an Amazon delivery station in Alpharetta, Georgia, Nov. 28, 2022. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images Amazon is taking its fight against a New York City delivery bill, which has been backed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani , to its shopping website and app. Some users who open the company's shopping app or website report being served with pop-ups and banners warning that the New York City Council "could add up to $5 per order" if it passes Intro 518, or the Delivery Protection Act. The bill would require Amazon to employ its army of third-party delivery companies directly, disrupting the contractor model it has relied on since 2018. Amazon uses a network of thousands of small companies, which often work solely for Amazon, to handle the last-mile portion of shipments, in an effort to speed up deliveries and control more of its logistics operations. "If this legislation passes, we'd no longer be able to work with them, and we'd be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city," Amazon's in-app message states. "That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees." The proposed legislation was introduced in February and is awaiting review by City Council Speaker Julie Menin. Amazon also posted a statement on its company website where it often publishes its policy positions . But rarely has the company used its valuable e-commerce site and app real estate to push its perspectives. Other tech companies including Uber and Lyft have similarly used their apps to advocate for or against legislation in the past. Amazon's pop-up notices and a stationary banner on its store homepage direct users to a form where they can "contact your council member to oppose Intro 518." The Delivery Protection Act has received a swell of support from labor groups, including the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, which has sought to unionize Amazon delivery and warehouse workers. Mamdani endorsed the bill in August, saying Amazon's subcontractor model "leaves workers vulnerable and corporations free to avoid accountability for reckless conditions on city streets." He's argued the bill would lead to safer working conditions for drivers, and allow the city to "regulate last-mile operations." Amazon has lobbied heavily against the bill, while business groups have launched local advertising campaigns, and warned they may sue the city if the bill passes. Trump bought Nvidia, Palantir, SpaceX in September as federal deals, White House ties grew
headlines.summary: President Trump disclosed purchases of Nvidia stock, SpaceX debt and Tesla shares in September, alongside millions of dollars in other investments.
headlines.article_text: Trump bought Nvidia, Palantir, SpaceX amid federal contracts Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points President Donald Trump's latest financial disclosure reveals 751 September trades worth between $40.9 million and $148.1 million, according to a CNBC analysis of the report. His accounts bought Palantir shares before $42.5 million in federal contract awards and invested in SpaceX around the time of a $946 million NASA contract expansion. Trump's accounts also bought Nvidia shares as then-CEO Jensen Huang strengthened his White House ties. The White House says Trump has no role in managing his investments. In this article NVDA TSLA PLTR Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT President Donald Trump attends a multilateral meeting with delegations from Japan, India and Australia at the Solaire Hotel in Manila, Philippines, Nov. 17, 2026. Win McNamee | Getty Images President Donald Trump's investment accounts bought shares of Nvidia , Palantir and Elon Musk's SpaceX in September, around the time the companies secured major federal contracts and their executives met with the president, according to a newly released financial disclosure. The 25-page filing shows 751 purchases and sales totaling between roughly $40.9 million and $148.1 million, according to a CNBC analysis. Purchases accounted for at least $29.2 million and sales at least $11.7 million. The filing reports transactions in broad dollar ranges, leaving the exact amounts and value of Trump's holdings unclear. Among the transactions were Palantir purchases before the company received two federal contracts worth $42.5 million combined according to contracting records, SpaceX investments shortly before and after a $946 million NASA contract expansion and Nvidia trades as its then-CEO, Jensen Huang , cultivated a close relationship with Trump . The trades underscore a striking feature of Trump's presidency: His personal fortune remains invested in companies whose fortunes his administration can shape. His accounts reported more than 21,000 trades in 2025 , compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term. Recent presidents have generally divested individual stocks or used blind trusts to avoid potential conflicts. The White House has told CNBC previously Trump and his family have no control over the trades, which outside financial managers handle independently . The Trump Organization says the arrangement is designed to avoid even the appearance of a conflict. There is no evidence Trump directed the transactions or that his managers knew government decisions in advance. White House spokesman Davis Ingle said Trump's portfolio is independently managed and that neither the president nor his family has any input on trades. "All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers," Ingle told CNBC. The Trump Organization did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Read more on Trump investments Trump bought up to $25 million in Meta and millions in SpaceX debt in August Trump’s municipal bond portfolio reaches as much as $1 billion as policy overlaps mount Trump disclosure shows 1,100 July trades, Microsoft and Amazon sales Trump’s oil investments have gained millions during Iran war as his accounts keep trading Trump’s foreign licensing business booms to $59.5 million as Gulf developers pay JPMorgan, Schwab and UBS manage millions in Trump’s $858 million investment portfolio Trump bought as much as $5 million in Axon stock before ICE sought $220 million Taser deal Company that bet big on Trump-backed crypto says its fortunes have improved Trump family got about $500M from crypto venture — but investors saw steep losses Trump Jr. calls banking a 'Ponzi scheme' that forced family to create crypto business The Trump family crypto empire looks to Asia: Eric Trump talks Bitcoin in Hong Kong Trump family says U.S. dollar needs an upgrade and they are the ones to do it The timing was particularly notable at Palantir, the artificial intelligence software maker whose technology is used by U.S. military, intelligence and civilian agencies. Trump's accounts bought between $15,001 and $50,000 in Palantir shares on Sept. 2, followed by another purchase of between $1,001 and $15,000 on Sept. 9. A week later, the Department of Housing and Urban Development awarded Palantir a contract with $10.4 million in initial obligations for AI-powered grant oversight and fraud detection. On Sept. 29, the Department of Homeland Security awarded Palantir another $32.1 million software contract , bringing the two awards to roughly $42.5 million. That same day, CEO Alex Karp joined Trump, Musk, Huang and other technology executives at the White House for a meeting on artificial intelligence . Trump's accounts also bought shares and debt in SpaceX in the weeks surrounding a major NASA contract award. On Sept. 1, the accounts purchased between $100,001 and $250,000 in SpaceX debt carrying a 5.35% interest rate. Eight days later, they bought between $1,001 and $15,000 in shares of the major NASA and Pentagon contractor. On Sept. 18, NASA announced a $946 million expansion of its SpaceX contract, adding three astronaut missions to the International Space Station and bringing the agreement's total value to $5.92 billion. The agency had signaled plans for additional missions in May. Six days after the announcement, Trump's accounts bought another $15,001 to $50,000 in SpaceX shares on the same day Musk attended Trump's White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping . The filing does not show whether the purchase came before or after the dinner. The trades followed an even larger SpaceX investment in August , when Trump's accounts bought between $1 million and $5 million in the company's debt just two days before he signed a policy aimed at expanding commercial space transportation. Trump's accounts also continued buying Nvidia shares as Huang drew closer to the president — a relationship now under congressional scrutiny over Huang's ties to a woman suspected of spying for China. The September filing shows four Nvidia purchases totaling between $152,004 and $380,000, including two on Sept. 2 worth as much as $350,000 combined. The accounts also sold between $1,001 and $15,000 in Nvidia shares on Sept. 24, the day Huang also attended the state dinner with Xi. The trades bring Trump's Nvidia transactions to at least 108 since his return to office in 2025, worth between $27.2 million and $97.9 million, extending a CNBC analysis published Monday . The relationship between the president and Nvidia's then-CEO has drawn fresh scrutiny after The New York Times reported that intelligence officials warned Trump about Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Trump has denied being briefed. Huang resigned Nov. 12 following revelations about his personal relationships. The September filing also shows substantial trading beyond the three companies. The largest reported transaction was a Sept. 23 purchase of between $5 million and $25 million in Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF shares. That same day, Trump's accounts sold between $1 million and $5 million each in Comcast , McDonald's , Home Depot and Fidelity National Information Services , along with between $500,001 and $1 million each in Nike and Constellation Brands . On the buy side, Trump's accounts purchased between $250,001 and $500,000 in TJX shares on each of two consecutive days, Sept. 15 and 16. They also bought between $117,004 and $330,000 in Tesla shares across four transactions, along with smaller investments in CoreWeave , Intel , Microsoft and Apple . The stock will trade under the ticker "ANT" after the company raised $81.3 billion in the IPO. The Claude creator sold 980 million shares at $83 a piece on Wednesday, lifting the size and price of its offering. The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. Highlights so far: Ashton Kutcher congratulates the AI lab Market cap tops $2 trillion in debut, putting it among the tech titans ANT stock pops in first trade Protesters gather outside the Nasdaq Daniela Amodei gives a shoutout to mom Dario Amodei addresses debt and landing an investment-grade credit rating Spotted: Executives sporting "Clawd" pins at Nasdaq Dario Amodei renews pledge to pace frontier AI development Retail demand for ANT was the largest in history Anthropic employees set to get rich CNBC's reporters are covering Anthropic's IPO live on air and online from our bureaus in San Francisco and Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, and from the Nasdaq in New York City. VIDEO 15:11 15:11 Watch CNBC’s full interview with Anthropic co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei 12 Min Ago Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley rake in fees from Anthropic IPO Wall Street banks are set to reap a huge windfall from Anthropic's IPO, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley among the biggest earners. The company disclosed in its latest SEC filing that it agreed to pay the banks $550 million, surpassing the roughly $500 million payday banks took in from SpaceX's IPO in June. — Annie Palmer 19 Min Ago Anthropic's partners take a victory lap Anthropic's investors and other partners are taking a victory lap upon the AI lab's successful debut. Investors Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed dedicated the front page of their websites to congratulating Anthropic, as did counsel Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati . Bessemer's Byron Deeter posted a thread on X detailing the backstory of the firm's investment in Anthropic. — Caleigh Keating 27 Min Ago Menlo Ventures has $25 billion aggregate position in Anthropic, partner Matt Murphy says Close-up of sign for Menlo Ventures, San Francisco, California, March 12, 2026. Smith Collection | Gado | Archive Photos | Getty Images Menlo Ventures partner Matt Murphy, an early Anthropic investor, said the firm's aggregate position in the AI company is around $25 billion. "Clearly the most epic return for Menlo Ventures in our history, and one of the top handful in the history of venture capital," Murphy told CNBC in an interview. "We feel grateful. We have over five LPs that we've delivered over a billion dollars of returns to, and at the end of the day, that's really our job." — Ashley Capoot 33 Min Ago Ashton Kutcher celebrates Anthropic IPO Michael Kovac Ashton Kutcher congratulated Dario Amodei and "the whole team at Anthropic" in a post on X shortly before the AI company's first trade. Kutcher co-founded Sound Ventures , a Los Angeles-based venture capital firm, which invested in Anthropic in 2023 and participated in several subsequent funding rounds. The VC firm also counts Guy Oseary, the legendary talent manager for musicians including Madonna, among its cofounders. Bloomberg reported that Sound Ventures owns roughly half a percent of Anthropic, citing sources familiar with the matter. Sound Ventures' stake is likely now worth billions of dollars after the company's lofty IPO. — Annie Palmer 38 Min Ago Bessemer's Deeter calls Anthropic IPO a "Google moment" Byron Deeter, a partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, called Anthropic 's IPO a " Google moment" for the frontier lab during CNBC's Halftime Report. At over $2 trillion in market capitalization, Anthropic has entered Google's ranks as one of the most valuable companies in the world, behind Apple , Microsoft , Nvidia , Alphabet (Google's parent company), and Amazon . But Deeter says Anthropic doesn't need to "dominate intelligence" in the same way that Google dominates search. The artificial intelligence ecosystem will see "multiple great businesses," Deeter says, adding that he expects Anthropic to continue to be a market leader while also pacing the frontier of AI model development. — Isabel O'Brien 42 Min Ago Anthropic’s governance structure Anthropic Co-Founder and CEO Dario Amodei speaks at Dreamforce 2026 summit in San Francisco, California, U.S., September 15, 2026. Carlos Barria | Reuters Anthropic has an unusual governance structure . The company is a public benefit corporation, which means it's required to balance the financial interest of stockholders, the best interests of those affected by its conduct and its "company purpose." Anthropic said in its prospectus that its purpose is to facilitate the "responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity." Anthropic's seven co-founders also wield a lot of power over the company. Prior to the completion of its offering, Anthropic issued a single share of Class F common stock to a limited liability company called "Founder LLC." Anthropic's co-founders are the sole members of Founder LLC, and the entity holds 50.1% of the voting power of the company's outstanding shares. Each co-founder sold 3.38 million shares in the IPO, according to the prospectus, for total proceeds of $1.96 billion. Additionally, Anthropic introduced an independent governance body called the " Long-Term Benefit Trust " in 2023, which has the authority to elect and remove the majority of the company's board of directors. — Ashley Capoot 54 Min Ago Anthropic's market cap tops $2 trillion in Nasdaq debut Anthropic opened with a market capitalization of nearly $2.01 trillion, behind only Apple , Microsoft , Nvidia , Alphabet and Amazon . — Ashley Capoot 1 Hour Ago Ben Bernanke is in the room Ben Bernanke T.J.
